newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas aims to match last yr result.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas aims to match last yr result.

text.p: Qantas Airways Ltd said on Thursday the outlook for the second half of the 1996/97 year (July-June) was mixed but the airline still aimed to at least match the result reported for the 1996 financial year.

Qantas said revenues were not expected to grow quickly, fuel prices were forecast to remain high and price competition was expected to continue in most markets. It said future capacity expansion would be limited by the rate of productivity gains and further refinements. "The outlook is therefore for relatively modest fleet expansion and an undiminished drive for efficiency improvements and cost reductions to increase profits."
Qantas, 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc, said cost cutting would concentrate on fundamentals, including labour rates, labour productivity and outsourcing of functions.
"Looking beyond 1996/97, the airline will continue to expand, but at a slower rate than the very high levels of the last three years," chairman Gary Pemberton said in a statement.
Passenger numbers had grown more than 32 percent and capacity by more than 27 percent since December 1993.
Qantas earlier reported a 2.1 percent increase in net profit to A$151.4 million for the half year to December 31, 1996 from the previous corresponding half.
Pemberton said the result confirmed earlier forecasts that profits would be maintained by more aggressive cost cutting to offset the anticipated slowdown in the rate of revenue growth.
Cost savings of A$237 million had been made in the half year, and full year cost savings were expected to exceed A$430 million.

Cost savings were achieved by improved aircraft utilisation; reductions in aircraft operating and handling costs of more than A$50 million; savings in property, sales and maketing support and other costs of A$60 milion; and more than A$90 million in labour related savings.
Pemberton said total revenue rose 2.5 percent while net passenger revenue was virtually stable. Eliminating the effect of currency changes, passenger revenue growth was 4.4 percent.

Domestic profits were down on the same period last year despite an increase in passenger numbers and market share. Domestic operations contributed A$88.2 million in earnings before interest and tax, compared with A$93.0 milion previously.
Pemberton said international operations contributed A$168.3 million in earnings before interest and tax, compared with A$163.3 million previously.
